title: Why is the Mona Lisa famous? A smile and a theft
description: Leonardo’s Mona Lisa was admired long before it vanished in 1911. Discover how soft paint, a puzzling smile and a theft helped turn it into a celebrity.

sections.title: A masterpiece became a celebrity
sections.html:
The Mona Lisa is famous for Leonardo da Vinci’s skill, its intriguing smile and centuries of admiration. Its theft in 1911 then brought a much wider audience.

The Louvre points to both the painting’s artistry and its eventful history. The smile helped; the newspaper headlines certainly did too.

sections.title: The edges are part of the trick
sections.html:
Look at the face. Instead of a hard outline, Leonardo used delicate changes between light and shadow. Thin layers of paint soften the edges.

This is sfumato, a smoky blending effect. The Louvre’s collection account explains how it helps give the figure and her subtle smile a sense of life.

sections.title: The day the wall had a gap
sections.html:
On 21 August 1911, the painting disappeared. Vincenzo Peruggia, a glazier who had worked at the Louvre, had stolen it.

The museum describes the uproar and the recovery: Peruggia tried to sell it to an Italian art dealer, who alerted the authorities. It was found in 1913, with its fame greater than before.

sections.title: She was already somebody
sections.html:
The theft did not turn an unknown painting into a masterpiece. Artists admired it in Leonardo’s lifetime; Giorgio Vasari praised it in his writing in 1550.

Artistic reputation came first. A real-life mystery helped spread that reputation much further.
